scenarios.name: baseline-rag-eval-four-metrics
scenarios.rationale: Both use EvaluationDataset.from_list with the current field names, the four metric instances, LLM and embeddings wrappers, and to_pandas() sorted by faithfulness, so B edges ahead on a slightly tighter worst-rows output and an isna check, while A adds a richer worst-answer display and NaN-first sorting.

scenarios.name: synthetic-testset-from-markdown-docs
scenarios.rationale: Both use TestsetGenerator with LangchainLLMWrapper/embedding wrappers, DirectoryLoader, generate_with_langchain_docs(testset_size=30) and to_pandas().to_csv, but B states more explicitly that the CSV lacks response/retrieved_contexts and shows running each user_input through the user's pipeline to fill them, while A covers this too but adds a TextLoader and extra caveats and is less direct in showing the pipeline loop (and claims the docs dir doesn't exist, unverified in the response text).

scenarios.name: ci-faithfulness-gate-pytest
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric more closely: it has a THRESHOLDS dict, a session-scoped fixture, a parametrized test, a CI secret, and the 40+ row advice. A has the same fixture and secret but uses two separate tests with env-var thresholds instead of a THRESHOLDS dict and a parametrized test, and only says 'more questions' without a number.
